invariants.assessment: Extends the single canonical kernel/runtime result path; no use-case-specific SWAP fork.
No file parsing, paths, formats or file units added to kernel/runtime production code.
Accepted exchange is a result field; parameters, state, forcing and numerics remain separate.
No new persistent per-column physical state; exchange values are interval results.
No solver scratch moved into persistent column state.
Scalar result additions do not constrain future SoA, pooling or batching layouts.
Rejected trials are excluded; only accepted routes publish accepted bottom-interface exchange.
No change to committed-state origin or warm-start rules; recomputation remains transaction-safe.
Exchange integration uses accepted step duration generically; no calendar boundary semantics.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced.
Adds an explicit accepted coupling result needed by later predictor-corrector orchestration without admitting that orchestration itself.
Does not weaken typed groundwater head/flux contracts; no end-to-end interface equality claim is made here.
Mass tolerance remains absent; accepted exchange follows the same exact accepted bottom-flux contribution.
Existing interface sensitivity remains separate and unchanged; no regression to finite-difference-only production policy.
No extra full SWAP runs are introduced by the result transport.
Constant-size result transport is compatible with MultiSWAP batching and does not add heavy solver instances.
No MODFLOW-cell or tile-fraction assumptions are introduced.
No deep-vadose interpretation or state is added inside SWAP.
No cross-component storage transfer logic is changed.
Exchange result is carried above soil-water solver internals and does not bind architecture to one Richards implementation.
Reuses existing accepted backend bottom flux; no duplicate physics implementation.
No consumer is coupled to HeadCalc internal arrays or solver implementation details.
No physical option or numerical policy is silently changed.
No unbounded retry or solver-cost behavior is added; only already accepted trajectory results are transported.
Reference behavior remains available and the admission replays O0/O2 independent qualification.
Availability and accepted exchange are explicit runtime-result diagnostics rather than hidden state.
No optional module allocation or state cost is introduced.
Runtime/coupler composition responsibilities, including tiles and external routing, remain outside the SWAP kernel.
Admission delta introduces no .swp, MODFLOW, midnight, fixed-day or external-file assumptions.
This F-CI55 audit and CI gate explicitly qualify the change against all 30 invariants before canonical promotion.

hard_nonclaims: No crash-recovery, distributed-runtime or throughput qualification.
